input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: § 12.4 imposes a post-term non-compete on Customer for 24 months, worldwide ("in any territory"), covering any product or service that "competes with Vendor" — undefined scope and beyond the 12-month walk-away limit. It binds our party (not the Vendor) and restricts our ability to develop, buy, or sell products, which the playbook rejects outright. It also contradicts § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no non-compete commitment. Preferred remedy is deletion; a named-product, term-only, 12-month restriction with internal-development and acquisition carve-outs is the fallback if Vendor presses.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept restrictions on the businesses we operate or the products we buy or build, so we have deleted the 24-month worldwide non-compete in § 12.4; it also directly contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no non-compete commitment. If Vendor needs protection for a specific offering, we could consider a narrow restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only and capped at 12 months, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
proposal.summary: Delete the 24-month worldwide non-compete binding Customer in § 12.4.
